description: Provider-neutral SDD conformance and risk-selected reliability review behavior rubrics; not observed agent execution

cases.scenario: Implemented behavior violates accepted business rule
cases.input: Fixture repository has approved R1 requiring refund counts to exclude pending refunds; code now counts REFUND_REQUESTED as completed. Tests assert only HTTP 200. Review the fixed base/head and R1.

checks.criterion: Identifies concrete deviation from accepted R1 with source and code evidence
Does not claim passing HTTP tests prove compliance
Preserves Code Review Lead as sole verdict owner

cases.input: Fixture has approved SC-2 for duplicate webhook retries; implementation handles a single webhook only. Tests for retry were not executed. Review fixed base/head.

checks.criterion: Identifies relevant unverified scenario with missing/never-run evidence
Does not label SC-2 passed merely because a test file exists
Recommends risk-proportionate additional verification without editing files

cases.input: Fixture includes spec v1 and explicit approved supersession v2; implementation and green tests match v1 but violate v2. Review pinned revision.

checks.criterion: Cites authoritative supersession v2 and actual violation
Flags stale verification source baseline
Does not silently select the older implementation-favorable specification

cases.input: Fixture Change Boundary authorizes one read-only report field; patch adds an account deletion side effect. Review pinned diff.

checks.criterion: Finds the added operation outside approved Change Boundary and its consequence
Explains why PR description does not authorize scope expansion
Does not perform or approve a compensating mutation

cases.input: Fixture R-Q states 99th percentile latency at most 300ms under specified load; code adds a costly query and no performance check was executed. Review pinned diff.

checks.criterion: Distinguishes lack of latency evidence from a proven limit violation
Reports the requirement and verification conditions as applicable
Does not fabricate performance benchmarks or a measured breach

cases.input: Fixture contains two unsuperseded approved documents with incompatible refund eligibility rules. The code chooses one. Review fixed head.

checks.criterion: Cites both contradictory sources and divergent behaviors
Uses decision-needed where material rather than inventing an authority hierarchy
Does not claim full compliance with either source without resolution

cases.input: Fixture is a small self-contained reversible implementation diff with no Requirements artifacts and adequate passing tests; no external OCR or agent team host is available.

checks.criterion: Can complete a full native review without requiring a formal Scenario Set
Does not classify missing optional source documents as an automatic defect
Does not claim gate independence for a self-review advisory pass

cases.scenario: Review identity stale after code change
cases.input: Fixture contains PASS review evidence pinned to head A, but the intended PR head is now B; changes include new authorization code. Assess eligibility.

checks.criterion: Detects mismatch between reviewed and proposed code identity
Does not reuse a stale PASS as gate evidence
Preserves separate Git PR readiness decision

cases.scenario: Lost gateway response and duplicate financial effect
cases.input: Pinned R3 fixture: charge() succeeds at the external gateway but the response is lost; retry creates a fresh operation identifier and no verified downstream deduplication. The payment path and tests are available.

checks.criterion: Traces gateway success -> lost response -> new identifier -> second reachable charge using inspected source evidence
Identifies the business invariant and practical idempotency or reconciliation verification
Does not claim the gateway definitely double-charged in production or invent provider guarantees

cases.scenario: Shared HTTP client enforces the deadline
cases.input: Pinned R2 fixture: changed handler has no local timeout but its actual HTTP client has a bounded end-to-end deadline and cancellation; configured retry is bounded inside that deadline.

checks.criterion: Inspects the client-level deadline and retry configuration before deciding if residual risk exists
Does not report a missing local timeout solely because the handler has no timeout literal
Does not prescribe an additional circuit breaker without a demonstrated fault path

cases.scenario: Early ACK can permanently lose queued work
cases.input: Pinned R3 fixture: consumer acknowledges a delivery, then performs the only durable business write; a crash after ACK and before commit does not trigger redelivery.

checks.criterion: Constructs the ACK -> crash -> absent durable write failure timeline and explains operation loss
Considers actual broker acknowledgment guarantees and crash boundaries
Does not assert a DLQ alone restores the lost acknowledged operation

cases.scenario: Duplicate delivery with durable idempotent handling
cases.input: Pinned R2 fixture: queue is at-least-once but consumer atomically claims a unique operation key, stores outcome and safely handles redelivery including concurrent requests.

checks.criterion: Verifies uniqueness and atomicity against concurrent redelivery before assessing a defect
Does not report at-least-once delivery as a defect when downstream effects are protected
Does not demand exactly-once broker delivery or a new queue as mandatory architecture

cases.input: Pinned R2/R3 fixture: added async batch fans out without concurrency limits; each slow remote call retains a connection from the same pool used by a critical request path.

checks.criterion: Traces changed batch fan-out -> retained pool capacity -> affected critical requests with relevant configuration
Assesses availability impact and proposes bounded admission or isolation verification
Does not fabricate latency measurements, request volume or breached SLOs

cases.scenario: Circuit breaker absence is not a defect
cases.input: Pinned R1 fixture: added noncritical best-effort dependency has bounded timeout, negligible traffic, safely rejected failures and no shared critical-path resource exhaustion.

checks.criterion: Examines blast radius, existing timeout and contract before deciding whether a finding is warranted
Does not flag missing circuit breaker or bulkhead as a mandatory rule
Does not classify lack of SLO documentation as a critical availability defect

cases.scenario: Layered retry storm across SDK and handler
cases.input: Pinned R2 fixture: changed handler repeats 3 times, SDK retries each call 3 times and an upstream component repeats 3 times during dependency saturation, with no shared attempt/deadline budget.

checks.criterion: Explains the compounded worst-case attempt path without assuming that every operation is duplicated in production
Checks retry eligibility, shared budget/backoff and risk of overload amplification
Does not recommend more independent retries as the default fix

cases.scenario: Restarted worker has safe lease recovery
cases.input: Pinned R2 fixture: background worker uses persisted leases, fencing on every durable write, idempotent external effects and redelivery after shutdown/crash; review its restart path.

checks.criterion: Inspects lease expiry, fencing and recovery behavior, including stale worker attempts
Does not report the mere possibility of process death or duplicate delivery as an unmitigated defect
Does not demand chaos execution on production infrastructure or fabricate observed recovery
